questions.stem: $\lim\limits_{x \to \infty} \left\{x - \sqrt[n]{(x - a_{1})(x - a_{2})\ldots(x - a_{n})}\right\}$ where $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ are positive rational numbers. The limit
questions.solution:
$\lim\limits_{x \to \infty} \left\{x - \sqrt[x]{(x - a_{1})(x - a_{2})\ldots(x - a_{n})}\right\}$
$\lim\limits_{x \to \infty} \left\{x - x^{n}\sqrt{\left(1 - \frac{a_{1}}{x}\right)\left(1 - \frac{a_{2}}{x}\right)\ldots\left(1 - \frac{a_{n}}{x}\right)}\right\}$
$\Rightarrow \lim\limits_{x \to \infty} x\left\{1 - \left(1 - \frac{a_{1}}{x}\right)^{1/n}\left(1 - \frac{a_{2}}{x}\right)^{1/n}\ldots\left(1 - \frac{a_{n}}{x}\right)^{1/n}\right\}$
$\Rightarrow \lim\limits_{x \to \infty} x\left[1 - \left(1 - \frac{a_{1}}{nx}\right)\left(1 - \frac{a_{2}}{nx}\right)\ldots\left(1 - \frac{a_{n}}{xn}\right)\right]$
$\Rightarrow \lim\limits_{x \to \infty} x\left[\frac{a_{1} + a_{2} + \ldots + a_{n}}{nx}\right] = \frac{a_{1} + a_{2} + \ldots + a_{n}}{n}$

questions.stem: Suppose $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be given by $f(x) = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if } x = 1 \\ e^{(x^{10} - 1)} + (x - 1)^{2}\sin\frac{1}{x - 1}, & \text{if } x \neq 1 \end{cases}$ then
questions.solution:
$f : R \to R\ f(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } x = 1 \\ e^{(x^{10} - 1)} + (x - 1)^{2}.\sin\left(\frac{1}{x - 1}\right) & \text{if } x \neq 1 \end{cases}$
$f(1^{-}) = 1 + 0 = 1$
$f(1^{+}) = 1 + 0 = 1$
$f(1) = 1$
$\therefore$ f(x) is continuous at x = 1
$f'(x) = \left\{e^{(x^{10} - 1)}.(10x^{5}) + 2(x - 1).\sin\left(\frac{1}{x - 1}\right) - (x - 1)^{2}.\cos\left(\frac{1}{x - 1}\right).\left(\frac{1}{x - 1}\right)^{2}\right\}$
which does not exist.

questions.stem: Let $f : [1, 3] \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous and be derivable in (1, 3) and $f'(x) = [f(x)]^{2} + 4\ \forall x \in (1, 3)$. Then
f(x) is a differentiable function and given $f'(2) = 6$ and $f'(1) = 4$, then $L = \lim\limits_{h \to 0} \frac{f(2 + 2h + h^{2}) - f(2)}{f(1 + h - h^{2}) - f(1)}$
questions.solution:
$\lim\limits_{h \to 0} \frac{f(2 + 2h + h^{2}) - f(2)}{f(1 + h - h^{2}) - f(1)}$  $\left[\frac{0}{0} \text{ (form)}\right]$
by L. Hospital rule.
$\lim\limits_{h \to 0} \frac{f'(2 + 2h + h^{2})(2h + 2)}{f'(1 + h - h^{2})(1 - 2h)} = \frac{f'(2)}{f'(1)} \times \left(\frac{2}{1}\right)$
$= \frac{6}{4} \times 2 = 3$

questions.stem: Let $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{b}\right) = \log_{e}\left(\frac{x}{n}\right)^{n}$, then $Ay_{2} + By_{1} + Cy = 0$ is possible for
questions.solution:
$\frac{-1}{\sqrt{1 - \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}}} \times \frac{1}{b}y_{1} = \left(\frac{n}{n \times \frac{x}{n}}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-1\ y_{1}}{\sqrt{b^{2} - y^{2}}} = \frac{n}{x}$
$\Rightarrow y_{1}x + n\sqrt{b^{2} - y^{2}} = 0$
$\Rightarrow y_{1} + xy_{2} + \frac{n}{2\sqrt{b^{2} - y^{2}}}.(-2y)y_{1} = 0$
$\Rightarrow y_{1} + xy_{2} + \frac{n^{2}}{x}y = 0$
$\Rightarrow y_{1}x + x^{2}y_{2} + n^{2}y = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2}y_{2} + xy_{1} + n^{2}y = 0$
$A = x^{2}, B = x, C = n^{2}$

questions.stem: If $I = \int \frac{x^{2}dx}{(x\sin x + \cos x)^{2}} = f(x) + \tan x + c$, then $f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
$I = \int \frac{x^{2}}{(x\sin x + \cos x)^{2}}dx = \int \frac{x}{(x\sin x + \cos x)^{2}} \times \frac{x}{\cos x}dx$
$I = -\frac{1}{(x\sin x + \cos x)}.\frac{x}{\cos x} + \int \frac{1}{(x\sin x + \cos x)}.\frac{(\cos x + x\sin x)}{\cos^{2}x}dx$
$I = -\frac{1}{(x\sin x + \cos x)}.\frac{x}{\cos x} + \int \sec^{2}x\,dx$
$I = -\frac{x}{(x\sin x + \cos x)\cos x} + \tan x + C$
$\therefore f(x) = \frac{-x}{\cos x(xisnx + C)}$

The value of $\int_{0}^{1/2} \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2n}}}$ is $(n \in \mathbb{N})$
questions.solution:
For 0 to $\frac{1}{2}$
$x^{2} \geq x^{2n}$
$\Rightarrow -x^{2} \leq -x^{2n}$
$\Rightarrow 1 - x^{2} \leq 1 - x^{2n}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}} \geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2n}}}$

questions.stem: If $I_{n} = \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos^{n}x\cos nx\,dx$, then $I_{1}, I_{2}, I_{3} \ldots$ are in
questions.solution:
$I_{n} = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^{n}x.\cos nx\,dx$
$I_{1} = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos x.\cos x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \left(\frac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\right)dx = \frac{\pi}{4}$
$I_{2} = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^{2}x.\cos 2x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} -\sin^{2}x.\cos 2x\,dx$
$2I_{2} = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^{2}2x = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{1 + \cos 4x}{2}dx = \frac{\pi}{4}$
$\therefore I_{2} = \frac{\pi}{8}$
$I_{3} = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^{3}x.\cos 3x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \left(\frac{3\cos x + \cos 3x}{4}\right)\cos 3x\,dx$
$= \frac{3}{4}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos x.\cos 3x\,dx + \frac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^{2}3x\,dx$
$= \frac{3}{8}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} (\cos 2x + \cos 4x)dx + \frac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{1 + \cos 6x}{2}dx$
$= \frac{\pi}{16}$
$\therefore I_{1}, I_{2}, I_{3}$ are in G.P.

questions.stem: If $y = \frac{x}{\log_{e}|cx|}$ is the solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{x} + \phi\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)$, then $\phi\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)$ is given by
questions.solution:
$y = \frac{x}{\ln|cx|}$
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\ln|cx| - 1}{(\ln|cx|)^{2}} = \frac{1}{\ln|cx|} - \frac{1}{(\ln|cx|)^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{x} - \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{2}$   $\therefore \phi\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = -\frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}$

questions.stem: The function $y = e^{kx}$ satisfies $\left(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dy}{dx} - y\right) = y\frac{dy}{dx}$. It is valid for
questions.solution:
$y = e^{kx}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = ke^{kx} = ky \Rightarrow \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = k^{2}e^{kx} = k^{2}y$
Now LHS
$= \left(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dy}{dx} - y\right) = (k^{2}y + ky)(ky - y) = k(k + 1)(k - 1)y^{2} = k(k^{2} - 1)y^{2}$
Now RHS $y\frac{dy}{dx} = ky^{2}$, A/q $k(k^{2} - 1)y^{2} = ky^{2} \Rightarrow k\left[k^{2} - 2\right] = 0 \Rightarrow k = 0, k = \pm\sqrt{2}$

questions.stem: Given $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \cot x\frac{dy}{dx} + 4y\,\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x = 0$. Changing the independent variable x to z by the substitution $z = \log\tan\frac{x}{2}$, the equation is changed to
questions.solution:
$\frac{dz}{dx} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sec^{2}(x/2)}{\tan(x/2)} = \frac{1}{\sin x} = \mathrm{cosec}\,x$
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{dz}.\frac{dz}{dx} = \mathrm{cosec}\,x\frac{dy}{dz}$, $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = \frac{d}{dz}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dz}{dx}\right)$
$= \frac{d}{dz}\left(\mathrm{cosec}.\frac{dy}{dz}\right)\mathrm{cosec}\,x$
$= \left(\mathrm{cosec}\,x\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - \mathrm{cosec}\,x.\cot x\frac{dx}{dz}\frac{dy}{dz}\right)\mathrm{cosec}\,x = \mathrm{cosec}^{2}x\frac{d^{2}y}{dz^{2}} - \mathrm{cosec}\,x.\cot x\frac{dy}{dz}$
$\therefore \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \cot x\frac{dy}{dx} + 4y\,\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x = 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{cosec}^{2}x\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - \mathrm{cosec}\,x.\cot x\frac{dy}{dz} + \cot x.\mathrm{cosec}\,x.\frac{dy}{dz} + 4\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x = 0$
$\Rightarrow \frac{d^{2}y}{dz^{2}} + 4y = 0$

questions.stem: A missile is fired from the ground level rises x meters vertically upwards in t sec, where $x = 100t - \frac{25}{2}t^{2}$. The maximum height reached is
questions.solution:
$x = 100t - \frac{25}{2}t^{2}$
$\frac{dx}{dt} = 100 - 25t$ for maximum and minimum $\frac{dx}{dt} = 0 \Rightarrow t = 4\ \mathrm{sec}$
$\frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}} = -25 < 0$
$\therefore$ at $x = 4$ it will have maixmum height
$x_{max} = 100 \times 4 - \frac{25}{2} \times 16 = 400 - 200 = 200\mathrm{m}$

Reflection of the line $\bar{a}z + a\bar{z} = 0$ in the real axis is given by
questions.solution:
Let, $a = \alpha + i\beta$ and $z = x + iy$
$\therefore \bar{a}z + a\bar{z} = 0$
$\Rightarrow (\alpha - i\beta)(x + iy) + (\alpha + i\beta)(x - iy) = 0$
$\Rightarrow 2(\alpha x + \beta y) = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha x + \beta y = 0$ which passes through origin $\therefore$ slope $= -\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$
$\therefore$ Reflected line's slope $= \frac{\alpha}{\beta}$
$\therefore$ Reflected line's equation : $\alpha x - \beta y = 0$
$\Rightarrow \left(\frac{a + \bar{a}}{2}\right)x - \left(\frac{a - \bar{a}}{2i}\right)y = 0$
$\Rightarrow \left(\frac{a + \bar{a}}{2}\right)\left(\frac{z + \bar{z}}{2}\right) - \left(\frac{a - \bar{a}}{2i}\right)\left(\frac{z - \bar{z}}{2i}\right) = 0$
$\Rightarrow az + \bar{a}\bar{z} = 0$
$\Rightarrow az + \overline{az} = 0$

questions.stem: The number of ways in which the letters of the word 'VERTICAL' can be arranged without changing the order of the vowels is
questions.solution:
Vowels 'EIA' to be kept in order, so out of 8 places 3 places can be chosen in ${}^{8}C_{3}$ ways. Remaining 5 letters can be arranged in $5!$ ways.
$\therefore$ Total number of ways $= {}^{8}C_{3} \times 5! = \frac{8!}{3!}$

questions.stem: n objects are distributed at random among n persons. The number of ways in which this can be done so that at least one of them will not get any object is
questions.solution:
Total number of ways of distributing n objects randomly among n persons $= n^{n}$
Number of ways in which each person gets exactly one object $= {}^{n}P_{n} = n!$
$\therefore$ Required number of ways $= n^{n} - n!$

questions.stem: Let A and B are orthogonal matrices and $\det A + \det B = 0$. Then
questions.solution:
$AA^{T} = I$ and $BB^{T} = I$
$\Rightarrow \det(AA^{T}) = 1$ and $\det(BB^{T}) = 1$
$\det(A) = -\det(B)$ (Given) $\Rightarrow (\det(A))^{2} = 1$   $\Rightarrow (\det(B))^{2} = 1$
$\therefore \det(A + B) = \det(A(B^{T} + A^{T})B)$
$= -\det(B^{T} + A^{T})$  $\left[\because (\det(A))(\det(B)) = -1\right]$ as $\det(A) = -\det(B)$
$= -\det(B + A)^{T}$
$= -\det(A + B)^{T}$
$= -\det(A + B)$
$\Rightarrow 2\det(A + B) = 0$
$\Rightarrow \det(A + B) = 0$
$\therefore (A + B)$ is singular

Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $ax^{2} + bx + c = 0$, a, b, c real and $s_{n} = \alpha^{n} + \beta^{n}$ and $\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 + s_{1} & 1 + s_{2} \\ 1 + s_{1} & 1 + s_{2} & 1 + s_{3} \\ 1 + s_{2} & 1 + s_{3} & 1 + s_{4} \end{vmatrix} = k\frac{(a + b + c)^{2}}{a^{4}}$ then $k =$
questions.solution:
$\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 + s_{1} & 1 + s_{2} \\ 1 + s_{1} & 1 + s_{2} & 1 + s_{3} \\ 1 + s_{2} & 1 + s_{3} & 1 + s_{4} \end{vmatrix}$
$= \begin{vmatrix} 1 + 1 + 1 & 1 + \alpha + \beta & 1 + \alpha^{2} + \beta^{2} \\ 1 + \alpha + \beta & 1 + \alpha^{2} + \beta^{2} & 1 + \alpha^{3} + \beta^{3} \\ 1 + \alpha^{2} + \beta^{2} & 1 + \alpha^{3} + \beta^{3} & 1 + \alpha^{4} + \beta^{4} \end{vmatrix}$
$= \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \alpha & \beta \\ 1 & \alpha^{2} & \beta^{2} \end{vmatrix} \times \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \alpha & \alpha^{2} \\ 1 & \beta & \beta^{2} \end{vmatrix}$
$= \{(1 - \alpha)(\alpha - \beta)(1 - \beta)\}^{2}$
$= (1 - (\alpha + \beta) + \alpha\beta)^{2}(\alpha - \beta)^{2}$
$= \left(1 + \frac{b}{a} + \frac{c}{a}\right)^{2}\left(\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} - \frac{4c}{a}\right)$
$= \frac{(a + b + c)^{2}}{a^{2}} \times \frac{b^{2} - 4ac}{a^{2}} = (b^{2} - 4ac)\frac{(a + b + c)^{2}}{a^{4}}$
$\therefore k = b^{2} - 4ac$

questions.stem: Let A and B are two independent events. The probability that both A and B happen is $\frac{1}{12}$ and probability that neither A nor B happen is $\frac{1}{2}$. Then
questions.solution:
$P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{12}$   $\Rightarrow P(A)P(B) = \frac{1}{12}$ ----------(1)
$P(A' \cap B') = \frac{1}{2}$   $\Rightarrow P(A \cup B) = 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$
$\Rightarrow P(A) + P(B) - P(A)P(B) = \frac{1}{2}$
$\Rightarrow P(A) + P(B) = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{7}{12}$
From (1), $P(A)\left(\frac{7}{12} - P(A)\right) = \frac{1}{12}$
$\Rightarrow P(A)^{2} - \frac{7}{12}P(A) + \frac{1}{12} = 0$
$\Rightarrow 12P(A)^{2} - 7P(A) + 1 = 0$
$\Rightarrow 12P(A)^{2} - 4P(A) - 3P(A) + 1 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (3P(A) - 1) - (4P(A) - 1) = 0$
$\therefore P(A) = \frac{1}{3}$ or $P(A) = \frac{1}{4}$
$\therefore P(B) = \frac{1}{12} \times 3 \Rightarrow P(B) = \frac{1}{12} \times 4$
$= \frac{1}{4}$   $= \frac{1}{3}$
$\therefore P(A) = \frac{1}{3}, P(B) = \frac{1}{4}$

questions.stem: The tangent at point $(a\cos\theta, b\sin\theta)$, $0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$, to the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ meets the x-axis at T and y-axis at $T_{1}$. Then the value of $\min\limits_{0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}} (OT)(OT_{1})$ is

questions.stem: Let $A(2\sec\theta, 3\tan\theta)$ and $B(2\sec\phi, 3\tan\phi)$ where $\theta + \phi = \frac{\pi}{2}$ be two points on the hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{4} - \frac{y^{2}}{9} = 1$. at B

questions.stem: If the lines joining the focii of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ where $a > b$, and an extremity of its minor axis is inclined at an angle $60^\circ$, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is

questions.stem: If the distance between the plane $ax - 2y + z = k$ and the plane containing the lines $\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{3} = \frac{z - 3}{4}$ and $\frac{x - 2}{3} = \frac{y - 3}{4} = \frac{z - 4}{5}$ is $\sqrt{6}$, then $|k|$ is

$\Rightarrow x - 2y + z = 0$ —— (1)
& given $\alpha x - 2y + z = k$ —— (2)
(1) // (2) $\Rightarrow \alpha = 1, k \ne 0$
$\therefore \frac{|k|}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{6} \Rightarrow |k| = 6$

questions.stem: $\int_{0}^{2\pi} \theta \sin^{6}\theta \cos\theta\, d\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_{0}^{2\pi} \theta \sin^{6}\theta \cos\theta\, d\theta$ .......(I)
applying King's Property,
$\int_{0}^{2\pi} (2\pi - \theta)\sin^{6}\theta . \cos\theta\, d\theta$ .........(II)
adding (I) and (II), $2I = 2\pi\int_{0}^{2\pi} \sin^{6}\theta \cos\theta\, d\theta$
$\Rightarrow I = \pi\int_{0}^{2\pi} \sin^{6}\theta \cos\theta$ .....(III)
Using Queen's Property, $\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx$, when $f(2a - x) = f(x)$
applying Queen's Property on (III), $I = 2\pi\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin^{6}\theta \cos\theta\, d\theta$
again, using Queen's Property, $\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 0$, when, $f(2a - x) = -f(x)$
$\boxed{I = 0}$

questions.stem: If $x = \sin\theta$ and $y = \sin k\theta$, then $(1 - x^{2})y_{2} - xy_{1} - \alpha y = 0$, for $\alpha =$
questions.solution:
$x = \sin\theta$
$y = \sin k\theta$
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta} = \frac{k\cos k\theta}{\cos\theta} = y_{1}$ .......(I)
$y_{2} = \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) \times \frac{d\theta}{dx} = \left[\frac{-k^{2}\sin(k\theta).\cos\theta + k\cos(k\theta)\sin\theta}{\cos^{2}\theta}\right] \times \frac{1}{\cos\theta}$
$y_{2} = \frac{k\cos(k\theta)\sin\theta - k^{2}\sin(k\theta)\cos\theta}{\cos^{3}\theta}$ ......(II)
also, $1 - x^{2} = 1 - \sin^{2}\theta = \cos^{2}\theta$ ...........(III)
So, putting the values of $1 - x^{2}$, $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ from (I), (II), (III) we get
$(1 - x^{2})y_{2} - xy_{1} = \alpha y$
$\Rightarrow (\cos^{2}\theta)\left[\frac{k\cos(k\theta)\sin\theta - k^{2}\sin(k\theta).\cos\theta}{\cos^{3}\theta}\right] - \frac{k\sin\theta\cos(k\theta)}{\cos\theta} = \alpha(\sin k\theta)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{k\cos(k\theta)\sin\theta - k^{2}\sin(k\theta)\cos\theta - k\sin\theta\cos(k\theta)}{\cos\theta} = \alpha\sin(k\theta)$
$\Rightarrow -k^{2}\sin(k\theta) = \alpha\sin(k\theta)$
So, $\boxed{\alpha = -k^{2}}$

questions.stem: In the interval $(-2\pi, 0)$, the function $f(x) = \sin\left(\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)$
questions.solution:
$x \in (-2\pi, 0)$, $f(x) = \sin\left(\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)$
$\because -2\pi < x < 0$
$\Rightarrow -8\pi^{3} < x^{3} < 0$
$\Rightarrow -\infty < \frac{1}{x^{3}} < -\frac{1}{8\pi^{3}}$
Hence, $\sin\left(\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)$ will take all values from $-1$ to 1, and will change its sign infinitely many times since it is a periodic function

options.text: changes sign more than once but finitely many times

questions.stem: The average ordinate of $y = \sin x$ over $[0, \pi]$ is
questions.solution:
As $\sin x$ is a continuous function in $[0, \pi]$
Average ordinate will be $= \frac{1}{\pi - 0}\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin x\, dx = \frac{[-\cos x]_{0}^{\pi}}{\pi} = \frac{2}{\pi}$

questions.stem: The portion of the tangent to the curve $x^{\frac{2}{3}} + y^{\frac{2}{3}} = a^{\frac{2}{3}}$, $a > 0$ at any point of it, intercepted between the axes
questions.solution:
for the given curve $x^{\frac{2}{3}} + y^{\frac{2}{3}} = a^{\frac{2}{3}}$, $a > 0$
Parametric Coordinates are $x = a\cos^{3}\theta$
$y = a\sin^{3}\theta$
$\frac{dy}{dx}$ = slope of tangent at any point $(x, y)$ $= \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}$
$= \frac{3a\sin^{2}\theta.\cos\theta}{3a\cos^{2}\theta(-\sin\theta)} = -\tan\theta$
Equation of tangent at $(a\cos^{3}\theta, a\sin^{3}\theta)$
$y - a\sin^{3}\theta = -\tan\theta(x - a\cos^{3}\theta)$
its x-intercept $= a\cos\theta$
its y-intercept $= a\sin\theta$
So, the tangent cuts the axes at $A(a\cos\theta, 0)$ and $B(0, a\sin\theta)$ respectively.
$AB = \sqrt{(a\cos\theta)^{2} + (a\sin\theta)^{2}} = a$, which is constant

options.text: varies as the product of abscissa and ordinate

questions.stem: If the volume of the parallelopiped with $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$, $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}$ and $\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$ as coterminous edges is 9 cu. units., then the volume of the parallelopiped with $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$, $(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \times (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})$ and $(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ as coterminous edges is
questions.solution:
Volume of Parallelopiped whose coterminous edges are $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c} = [\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]$
So, Given that $[\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\ \ \vec{b} \times \vec{c}\ \ \vec{c} \times \vec{a}] = 9 = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]$ (1)
$\therefore [\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}] = 3$ ...... (II)
Now volume of parallelopiped whose coterminous edges are
$(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$, $(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \times (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})$, $(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$
$\left[(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})\ \ (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \times (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})\ \ (\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})\right]$
$\left[\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\ \ \vec{b} \times \vec{c}\ \ \vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right]^{2}$
$= (9)^{2}$ (from (1))
$= 81$

questions.stem: Given $f(x) = e^{\sin x} + e^{\cos x}$. The global maximum value of $f(x)$
questions.solution:
$f(x) = e^{\sin x} + e^{\cos x}$
$f'(x) = 0$
$\Rightarrow e^{\sin x}.\cos x + e^{\cos x}(-\sin x) = 0$
$\Rightarrow e^{\sin x - \cos x} = \tan x$
$\boxed{x = \pi/4}$ or in general $\boxed{x = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}}$
Now, $f''(x) < 0$ at $x = \pi/4$ or $x = n\pi + \pi/4$
So, Global maximum exists at infinitely many points

options.text: exists at a point in $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and its value is $2e^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

questions.stem: Consider a quadratic equation $ax^{2} + 2bx + c = 0$ where a, b, c are positive real numbers. If the equation has no real root, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
For no real root
$(2b)^{2} - 4ac < 0$
$b^{2} < ac$
$b < \sqrt{ac}$ $\because a, b, c > 0$
If in AP, then $a + c = 2b$
i.e., $x = -1$ a solution
$\therefore$ a, b, c not in AP
$\because b^{2} < ac$
$\therefore$ a, b, c not in GP
For HP $b = \frac{2ac}{a + c} = \frac{2\sqrt{ac}}{\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}} + \sqrt{\frac{c}{a}}}$
$\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}} + \sqrt{\frac{c}{a}} \ge 2$
$\therefore \frac{2\sqrt{ac}}{\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}} + \sqrt{\frac{c}{a}}} \le 2$ $\therefore$ a, b, c in HP is possible

options.text: a, b, c cannot be in A.P. or H.P. but can be in G.P.
a, b, c cannot be in G.P. or H.P. but can be in A.P.
a, b, c cannot be in A.P. or G.P. but can be in H.P.
a, b, c cannot be in A.P., G.P. or H.P.

questions.stem: Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots, a_{n}$ be positive real numbers. Then the minimum value of $\frac{a_{1}}{a_{2}} + \frac{a_{2}}{a_{3}} + \ldots + \frac{a_{n}}{a_{1}}$ is

$AM \ge GM$ (property)
$\therefore$ Minimum value $= n$
It is possible when $a_{1} = a_{2} = a_{3} = \ldots = a_{n}$

questions.stem: The value of $\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left[\left(\frac{1}{2.3} + \frac{1}{2^{2}.3}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2^{2}.3^{2}} + \frac{1}{2^{3}.3^{2}}\right) + \ldots + \left(\frac{1}{2^{n}.3^{n}} + \frac{1}{2^{n+1}.3^{n}}\right)\right]$ is
questions.solution:
$\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\sum_{x=1}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{2^{x} \times 3^{x}} + \frac{1}{2^{x+1} \times 3^{x}}\right)$
$= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\sum_{x=1}^{n}\frac{1}{6^{x}}\left(1 + \frac{1}{2}\right)$
$= \frac{3}{2} \times \underbrace{\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{6^{2}} + \ldots + \frac{1}{6^{n}}\right)}_{\text{infinite GP}} = \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{1/6}{1 - 1/6} = \frac{3}{10}$

questions.stem: The family of curves $y = e^{a\sin x}$, where 'a' is arbitrary constant, is represented by the differential equation
questions.solution:

$\Rightarrow \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\log y}{\sin x}\right) = \frac{d}{dx}(a) \Rightarrow \frac{\sin x\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}{y} - \log y \times \cos x = 0$
$\Rightarrow y\log y = \tan x \times \frac{dy}{dx}$

questions.stem: Let f be a non-negative function defined on $\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$. If $\int_{0}^{x}\left(f'(t) - \sin 2t\right)dt = \int_{x}^{0} f(t)\tan t\,dt$, $f(0) = 1$, then $\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} f(x)\,dx$ is
questions.solution:
$f'(x) - \sin 2x = -f(x)\tan x$
$\Rightarrow f'(x) + \tan x\, f(x) = \sin 2x$
$\Rightarrow \frac{df(x)}{dx} + \tan x . f(x) = \sin 2x$
If $= e^{\int \tan x\,dx} = e^{\ln|\sec x|} = |\sec x| = \sec x$ As, $x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$
Solution is,
$f(x) \times \sec x = \int \sin 2x \sec x\,dx = \int 2\sin x\cos x\sec x\,dx = 2\int \sin x\,dx$
$f(x)\sec x = -2\cos x + C$
Put $x = 0$; $f(0) = 1$
$f(0)\sec 0 = -2\cos 0 + c$
$\Rightarrow 1 = -2 + C \quad \therefore C = 3$
$\therefore$ Required solution is;
$f(x)\sec x = -2\cos x + 3$
$f(x) = -2\cos^{2}x + 3\cos x$
$= -2\left(\frac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\right) + 3\cos x = -1 - \cos 2x + 3\cos x$
$f(x) = -1 - \cos 2x + 3\cos x$
Now $\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} f(x)\,dx$
$\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} (-1 - \cos 2x + 3\cos x)\,dx = \left[-x - \frac{\sin 2x}{2} + 3\sin x\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} = \left(-\frac{\pi}{2} + 3\right) - 0 = 3 - \frac{\pi}{2}$

questions.stem: A balloon starting from rest is ascending from ground with uniform acceleration of $4\ \mathrm{ft/sec^{2}}$. At the end of 5 sec, a stone is dropped from it. If T be the time to reach the stone to the ground and H be the height of the balloon when the stone reaches the ground, then

So, speed of ball when it's dropped
at point B is $v_{1} = 20$ ft/sec.
$S = v_{1}t + \frac{1}{2}a_{1}t^{2}$
$\Rightarrow -50 = 20t + \frac{1}{2}(-32)t^{2} \Rightarrow t = \frac{5}{2}$ sec
